body: To slightly narrow down the set of possibilities, does this vision transformer have any dynamism that may be unaccounted for (e.g., dyanmic shapes, control flow, or MoE)?

Re-posting @lw's investigation:

Through cuda-gdb we managed to identify that it comes from the CUDNN backend for SDPA during the backward pass. Here is all the info that I managed to gather : https://gist.github.com/eellison/c49ccad1cfe21be652273a6913a6984f

With that in mind, I tried to isolate that kernel from the tlparse output and managed to create a standalone minimal repro. See: https://gist.github.com/eellison/9f0b0a58522658288111fe13eb4f0f45

A few things to notice:

The IMA only seems to occur when we wrap that operator in a CUDA graph.

Enabling compute-sanitizer made the IMA disappear. Only cuda-gdb managed to give us insights

Disabling the CUDA caching allocator makes the graph capture throw an error. It looks as if that CUDNN operator detects that we're in capture mode and marks itself as unsupported. See https://gist.github.com/eellison/e4d97c9590fbd5f5222e6d92a7136faa

A version of #167101 is pretty hard to work with torch.compile? Torch.compile puts implementation selected during tracing into the trace, right? So if during tracing you'd have a seq len (dynamic) that's multipl of 128, you'll have something like `torch.ops.aten._scaled_dot_product_cudnn_attention_backward.` in the trace, and if at some point this dynamic size becomes non-multiple of 128 it's an IMA, or, if we correctly guard on seqlen, a recompile. cc @drisspg @eellison

So given that new cudnn version fixes this, I don't think we should spend much time for various torch.compile issues + old cudnn.

I'm having a bit of a hard time following, but I wanted to point out from a conversation with a colleague that the problem is (apparently) a use-after-free error for cuda stream capture originating here: https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/b372d39879d44c91a8d5b342022e74802b6a8da2/include/cudnn_frontend/graph_interface.h#L213-L217

Basically, by the time you execute the memcpy node (via cudaGraphLaunch), the host pageable memory from the std::vector<float> has died in host memory. I believe that the "proper" fix would be to use a cuda user object to retain a reference count to this host vector (or a copy of it) as long as the cudaGraphExec_t is alive, which can be done via [cuda user objects](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html#cuda-user-objects). But I want to be clear that I may be misunderstanding something. What's missing for me is that I personally am not sure what the alternative fix was in CUDNN > 9.15.

btw @atalman I checked https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/171532 locally and it would not fix the repro here as that specifically selects cuDNN (which would still be broken). This is expected, as the use would know what they are doing if they are manually selecting cuDNN. Disabling cuDNN by default is OK for 12.x wheels (just noting that it would not be reflected in the repro here)

You might need `compute-sanitizer` to see it reliably though e.g., `compute-sanitizer python3 script.py`

So realistically our options are
1) disable cudnn as default everywhere
2) update cudnn for 13.0 build, disable cudnn as default on 12.8, recommend 13 for blackwell
I much prefer 2. @eqy any known bugs in cudnn 9.15 that would cause us to delay update/not make update part of pytorch 2.10?

9.15.1 looks OK internally as well. There are grumblings from cuDNN's internal testing that there is a similar issue to https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/163539 for a _backward_ kernel but I have not been able to reproduce it locally (by extending the test we added for that issue to do backward). So we could be getting lucky and not hitting in in heuristics. Also FWIW to do a forward + backward 3d conv of that size is likely > 20 GiB even with a 16-bit wide dtype.

TLDR I don't have objections to #2, previously my understanding was @malfet and @atalman considered it too aggressive to bump both frontend and backend for 2.10 and we would recommend 13 (+nightly) for blackwell

My understanding is we are not bumping frontend, but with 9.15.1 it's fine?
Conv3d issue is unfortunate, but it must be present in 9.11 (or whatever pre-bump cudnn version was) too? In any case, at least 9.15.1 fixes forward issue so that's an improvement. 
12.8 for which we cannot update cudnn really becomes an orphan child, honestly it would be great to have a 12.x version for users who don't have 13.0 driver - I suspect even amont blackwell users there's a fair number on older driver, but that's not something we can fix for 2.10 I think.

We unfortunately need to bump frontend for this, here's as short of a summary as I can do:
+ frontend 1.15 introduced a workaround for non-modulo-64 sequence lengths that otherwise led to NaN in bprop, to fix https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/137347
+ unfortunately the workaround is not cudagraphs safe, leading to this IMA
+ 9.15.1+ doesn't need this workaround, but frontend < 1.16 doesn't know that

the above means we need 1.16+ and 9.15.1+
Thanks for the explanation! So how did it work on 13.0 in @atalman's message? Probably compute-sanitizer was required to get the reliable IMA?

        for _ in range(10):
                getitem_2659 = torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(cat_459, cat_461, permute_1393)

g.replay()
g.replay()
